issues: The passage specifies no location or writing materials; keep these visually unspecified.
The people are commanded to write, then the words are expounded after they have been written; do not depict writing and exposition as simultaneous.

The summary says Jesus “tells them” the prophetic words, but the verse specifies that he expounded the written words; the quotation is the words he told them, not an explicitly stated separate telling after the exposition.
“Those commanded to write” is a functional character label, not a source-given name or group description; the verse only says “them.”
The refiner/fire and soap imagery is figurative; any visual treatment should remain symbolic rather than stage a literal scene, as the notes specify.
The Lord and sons of Levi are mentioned in prophetic teaching, not described as present characters; their appearances are unspecified.
The offering and its participants are future prophetic content, not a narrated present event; the optional symbolic depiction should not imply a specific rite or historical occurrence.
The form and setting of the offering are unspecified.
The listed wrongdoing and judgment are in a prophetic warning, not a narrated present-tense event; visual symbolism should not become a specific incident or identify individuals.
The character label “God” is less precise than the source’s “Lord” and “Lord of Hosts”; the words themselves are correctly attributed in the dialogue.
The phrase “Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another” is a supplied quotation but is represented as narration despite being speech content; it does not invent words spoken.
The dialogue attribution “Unknown speaker” is not established by the verse; avoid assigning a speaker because the verse provides no speaker identification.
